posts.text:
Last major $SIVE disclosure was 100M CW DFB laser capacity Q4 2027. And a new foundry partner (that makes 2 including Win Semi).

Expected $JBL revenue coming in H1 2027 (with lasers for Jabil's 1.6T LRO scaling up H2 2027).

There's channel checks along the way like CIOE where Sivers was engaged with Chinese pluggable makers + laser ASPs being raised.

70mW/100mW ranges were the most tight to Chinese pluggable makers, which was surprising.

Biggest industry read through was $LITE selling out into 2029, making agreements for 2030, and having hyperscalers pay for capacity expansion for 2031. 

I don't think anyone has enough information to do any sort of accurate modeling for $SIVE like you can for $AAOI given they don't release product breakdown + capacity targets by quarter.

The 200mW NPO lasers Sivers is sampling is likely different ASP than your 70mW lasers shipped to pluggable makers. And your custom CPO lasers are different pricing too. 

Like all sampling/qualification players from $AEHR to $AAOI back in 2025, usually the risk/reward comes in whether qualifications convert and what new customers they have, which is always a risk. 

In a bull case, if $SIVE comes online with 300m laser supply (2:1 implied ratio, already has "tremendous" supply online from likely US fab) during a structural shortage.  

Pluggable players like $JBL, 6 other vendors.  

$GFS as the reference design laser for their CPO/NPO platform. 

Your minor players vendors like $POET, $AEVA and other players end up scaling.

And all the other custom products they hinted they were working on in the past for CPO years back.  

I think the probability that they cook is higher since there's so many ongoing qualifications during a bottleneck. 

We've already seen ownership changes from Swedish investors to US/International retail from $SIVE shareholder disclosures. 

My guess is that trends institutional from retail before US listing next year amid the market correction. 

Think people forgot institutions have already financed their expansion, which was a 700M SEK round 100%+ ago (multiple times oversubscribed). 

And that $SIVE uses primarily external fabs, so it's not the same as a lot of the major financing concerns affecting Neoclouds. 

Anyway, up to management execution, I'm not running Sivers so no clue what other companies are working with them now, whether it's Cambridge or some other US player like Semtec.

TLDR:

- Just need to wait for earnings for more disclosures around qualifications + partners, only so much public can guess from channel checks and supplier mapping. 

Not quite the same as $LITE CEO where you can see the guy on Fox news or Bloomberg interviews every week (which is a good thing)

Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi says unlike banks, he doesn't want to pocket the interest margin, and wants to give most of that yield back to customers

"As we're moving more into our own rails and infrastructure, we have to innovate and actually disrupt some of our existing products and make it where we make less money or we don't make money."

"When you think about fees or intermediaries or even things that we charge for over time, we have to be able to continue to bring that down or move on with a new business model, because someone else will actually go out and say, I don't want to rent-seek this."

"I think that ends up becoming a really important piece of any of these traditional institutions, which is how are they going to innovate moving forward?"

"The one thing we continue to hear is you need to be able to be a bank to be able to offer yield. Well, I'm not interested in the net interest margin for ourselves."

"In some cases, it'll be good for us. But in many cases, imagine bringing all that interest margin back to our customers. It's their yield."

"I just think that's just such a core piece of what you want to be able to do on behalf of your customers."

"Most fintechs are on UI rented on layers. Our goal has been, let's do the hard stuff first. Every layer we own, we can price toward costs and then give that to our customers."

"We're not doing any rent extraction. We're able to do it because we're on top of onchain or DeFi liquidity, depending on how it's built out. Because it moves on stablecoin rails today, instead of correspondent banks, you're removing that intermediary."

With afterburner, the F-16 exceeds at ~130 kN

But the fact this comparison even exists is insane

Tesla just pushed automotive engineering deep into aerospace territory

posts.name: 速溶猪 Yuxin
posts.text:
Token2049 期间，我受邀参加了火币的内部活动，做了一场 panel 分享，也出席了他们的 VIP 晚宴。另外和孙宇晨孙哥@justinsuntron 即兴约了一场采访，目前正在打磨问题。

**先替火币澄清一件事。晚宴原定 6 号，后来因为安排调整改到了 8 号。工作人员是真的尽心尽力，我亲眼看着他们为了协调好每一个人，焦灼地忙了全程。办过活动的人都知道，现场总有太多突发状况：场地临时变更，容纳人数跟着变，这些未知因素导致一些 VIP 没能到场。但团队自始至终都在积极解决问题。

火币的现场活动给我一种很不一样的感觉。在其他交易所的夹击之下，来到现场的反而都是火币多年的老用户，整场氛围其乐融融，非常家人向🙏感谢 @Ceee333_ 的邀请，她是这场活动的负责人之一，也是双语主持，业务能力相当过硬。还有@HTX_Molly @Lumibb_ @Xiaodu_HTX 等火币的小伙伴，每个人都很 energetic。这是我第一次深度接触火币的活动对接团队，评价很高（我不是托，是托死全家）。

**再说说我筹划的这场采访（目前身体太差的确稍微拖延了）。我有稍微看了下孙哥和邵艾伦那场”薄肌”采访，以及和自由潜冠军金明聊 Crypto、AI 与量子威胁的那场。我想问点不太一样的人文向问题，因为我的视角可能有些特别：我是从新概念时期就知道孙哥的。同为新概念作文大赛的获奖者，他某种程度上算是我的前辈。我第一次听到这个名字，是在《萌芽》上读到他写的《一道论证题》，所以对他的文青之路一路追踪非常熟稔。

我也注意到，孙哥提到他们生态里一直比较活跃的以太坊挖矿活动，所以也想专门问问他怎么看 ETH 这个资产。对于BTC被攻破这块，我和以太坊基金会做抗量子研究和在Yale/MIT读相关PHD的一些朋友交流过，他们对 Q-Day 的到来目前还算比较乐观，这个话题也想和他聊聊。

**最后一个小提议：**除了数学奖，火币很值得再设一个文学奖/人文奖。我感觉现在这些交易所办的这种访谈活动，基本上都是跟交易员对谈，来来回回，其实也都是那些交易员，同质化程度太高了，包括打广告的 KOL 也是，基本上是今天做完交易所 A 的广告，明天又去发交易所 B 的广告。孙哥既是新概念出身，又做过社交 App（陪我），某种程度上“薄肌”也算是一种文化输出了，那是否火币可以系统性以活动的形式支持更多元的加密文化输出？

先发散到这儿，抛砖引玉，之后再细聊。
